  127: export class GuestDocumentAccessService {
  128:   private readonly store: DocumentArchiveStore;
  129:   private readonly tableName: string;
  130:   private readonly ids: DocumentArchiveIdGenerator;
  131:   private readonly rateLimiter: DocumentArchiveGuestRateLimiter;
  132:   private readonly pepper: string;
  133:   private readonly now: () => string;
  134: 
  135:   constructor(deps: GuestDocumentAccessServiceDeps) {
  136:     this.store = deps.store;
  137:     this.tableName = deps.tableName;
  138:     this.ids = deps.ids;
  139:     this.rateLimiter = deps.rateLimiter;
  140:     this.pepper = deps.pepper;
  141:     this.now = deps.now ?? (() => new Date().toISOString());
  142:   }
  143: 
  144:   /** Issuance entry point - normally invoked by an authenticated internal flow when a
  145:    * DocumentRequest is created (recurrence's job, D-143 Decision 8, a separate follow-up task).
  146:    * Kept here as the minimal, explicit extension point this task needs: guest access cannot be
  147:    * exercised end to end without SOME way to mint a credential. */
  148:   async issueCredential(input: IssueCredentialInput): Promise<IssuedRequestAccessCredential> {
  149:     const issued = issueRequestAccessCredential(this.pepper);
  150:     const now = this.now();
  151:     const credential: RequestAccessCredential = {
  152:       ...requestAccessCredentialKey(issued.selectorHash),
  153:       entityType: "RequestAccessCredential",
  154:       selectorHash: issued.selectorHash,
  155:       secretHash: issued.secretHash,
  156:       tenantId: input.tenantId,
  157:       subjectId: input.subjectId,
  158:       requirementId: input.requirementId,
  159:       documentRequestId: input.documentRequestId,
  160:       tokenVersion: 1,
  161:       expiresAt: input.expiresAt,
  162:       purgeAfterTtl: epochSecondsFromIso(input.expiresAt),
  163:       createdAt: now,
  164:       updatedAt: now,
  165:       version: 1,
  166:     };
  167:     const created = await this.store.putIfAbsent(credential);
  168:     if (!created) {
  169:       // Astronomically unlikely selector collision (128 bits) - never silently overwrite an
  170:       // existing credential pointer.
  171:       throw new ValidationError("Could not issue credential (selector collision).");
  172:     }
  173:     return issued;
  174:   }
  175: 
  176:   /** Layer 1: validates a `RequestAccessCredential` token end to end. Never mints a session -
  177:    * callers that only need to SHOW request info (an interstitial page) call this alone. */
  178:   async resolveCredential(rawToken: string, requestContext: { ip: string }): Promise<ResolvedCredential> {
  179:     const parsed = parseRequestAccessToken(rawToken);
  180:     if (!parsed) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  181: 
  182:     const selectorHash = hmacRequestAccessCrypto.hash(this.pepper, parsed.selector);
  183: 
  184:     // Rate limit consumed BEFORE lookup, by both the selector (computable even if no pointer
  185:     // exists) and IP - Decision 4's multidimensional requirement, applied at the earliest point
  186:     // an oracle could otherwise form (same discipline as GuestSubmissionService.resolveToken).
  187:     try {
  188:       await this.rateLimiter.consumeBoth({ requestKey: selectorHash, ip: requestContext.ip, limit: RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE, windowSeconds: RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS });
  189:     } catch {
  190:       throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  191:     }
  192: 
  193:     const pointer = await this.store.get<RequestAccessCredential>(requestAccessCredentialKey(selectorHash));
  194: 
  195:     // Dummy anti-timing path - even when no pointer exists, still compute a hash and a
  196:     // timingSafeEqual comparison so response time never depends on selector existence. The dummy
  197:     // hash's fixed prefix can never collide with a real secretHash (issueRequestAccessCredential
  198:     // never produces this literal input).
  199:     const targetSecretHash = pointer?.secretHash ?? hmacRequestAccessCrypto.hash(this.pepper, `dummy:${selectorHash}`);
  200:     const secretOk = requestAccessSecretMatches(this.pepper, parsed.secret, targetSecretHash);
  201:     if (!pointer || !secretOk) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  202: 
  203:     if (pointer.revokedAt) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  204:     if (pointer.expiresAt < this.now()) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  205: 
  206:     const request = await this.store.get<DocumentRequest>(documentRequestKey(pointer.tenantId, pointer.subjectId, pointer.documentRequestId));
  207:     if (!request || !isDocumentRequestLive(request.status)) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  208:     // Re-validate against the live Request's deadline too (same "credential TTL OR deadline,
  209:     // whichever is sooner, re-checked at resolve time" discipline as GuestTokenPointer's D-037
  210:     // precedent) - catches a deadline edited after the credential was issued without reissuing it.
  211:     if (request.deadline && request.deadline < this.now()) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  212: 
  213:     if (request.status === "REQUESTED") await this.markOpened(request);
  214: 
  215:     return { credential: pointer, request };
  216:   }
  217: 
  218:   /**
  219:    * Discovery route (item 6 of D-173's estado-final-consolidado.md, engineering-only slice -
  220:    * see D-19x for the full contradiction/pendency writeup): lets a guest who has a valid
  221:    * credential token discover which `DocumentTypeId`s are currently valid to submit, WITHOUT any
  222:    * `authorize()`/`RequestContext` - same token-resolution discipline as `resolveCredential()`,
  223:    * reused here rather than duplicated. Only ACTIVE types are ever returned (never DRAFT/
  224:    * DEPRECATED) - a guest has no legitimate reason to see a type it cannot successfully submit
  225:    * against, since D-184's transactional ConditionCheck would reject anything else anyway.
  226:    * Read-only, no side effect (does NOT call `markOpened` - that is `resolveCredential`'s own
  227:    * concern and this route can be polled/refreshed by a guest UI without mutating Request state).
  228:    */
  229:   async listActiveDocumentTypesForGuest(rawToken: string, requestContext: { ip: string }): Promise<GuestDocumentTypeSummary[]> {
  230:     const parsed = parseRequestAccessToken(rawToken);
  231:     if (!parsed) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  232: 
  233:     const selectorHash = hmacRequestAccessCrypto.hash(this.pepper, parsed.selector);
  234:     try {
  235:       await this.rateLimiter.consumeBoth({ requestKey: selectorHash, ip: requestContext.ip, limit: RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE, windowSeconds: RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS });
  236:     } catch {
  237:       throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  238:     }
  239: 
  240:     const pointer = await this.store.get<RequestAccessCredential>(requestAccessCredentialKey(selectorHash));
  241:     const targetSecretHash = pointer?.secretHash ?? hmacRequestAccessCrypto.hash(this.pepper, `dummy:${selectorHash}`);
  242:     const secretOk = requestAccessSecretMatches(this.pepper, parsed.secret, targetSecretHash);
  243:     if (!pointer || !secretOk) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  244:     if (pointer.revokedAt) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  245:     if (pointer.expiresAt < this.now()) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  246: 
  247:     const request = await this.store.get<DocumentRequest>(documentRequestKey(pointer.tenantId, pointer.subjectId, pointer.documentRequestId));
  248:     if (!request || !isDocumentRequestLive(request.status)) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  249:     if (request.deadline && request.deadline < this.now()) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  250: 
  251:     // Same GSI1 DOCTYPESTATUS namespace as DocumentArchiveService.listDocumentTypes, read
  252:     // directly against the store (never through that authorize()-gated method - this whole
  253:     // module never calls authorize()/RequestContextResolver, see file header). Catalogs are
  254:     // small (a handful to low hundreds of types per tenant), so - unlike the internal
  255:     // paginated-by-design admin listing - this accumulates every page here: a guest-facing
  256:     // discovery list has no caller-driven cursor to hand back, and a hard page cap (`MAX_PAGES`)
  257:     // bounds the cost of a pathological tenant rather than looping unbounded.
  258:     const MAX_PAGES = 20;
  259:     const items: DocumentType[] = [];
  260:     let exclusiveStartKey: Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
  261:     for (let page = 0; page < MAX_PAGES; page++) {
  262:       const result = await this.store.queryIndexPage<DocumentType>({
  263:         indexName: "GSI1",
  264:         partitionKeyValue: `TENANT#${pointer.tenantId}#DOCTYPESTATUS#ACTIVE`,
  265:         exclusiveStartKey,
  266:       });
  267:       items.push(...result.items);
  268:       if (!result.lastEvaluatedKey) break;
  269:       exclusiveStartKey = result.lastEvaluatedKey;
  270:     }
  271: 
  272:     return items.map((item) => ({ documentTypeId: item.documentTypeId, displayName: item.displayName }));
  273:   }
  274: 
  275:   /** Layer 2: the ONLY way a GuestSession is minted - always an explicit call, never a side
  276:    * effect of `resolveCredential`. */
  277:   async startGuestSession(rawToken: string, requestContext: { ip: string }): Promise<StartGuestSessionResult> {
  278:     const resolved = await this.resolveCredential(rawToken, requestContext);
  279:     const issued = issueGuestSession(this.pepper);
  280:     const now = this.now();
  281:     const expiresAt = new Date(Date.parse(now) + GUEST_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS * 1000).toISOString();
  282:     const session: GuestSession = {
  283:       ...guestSessionKey(issued.selectorHash),
  284:       entityType: "GuestSession",
  285:       selectorHash: issued.selectorHash,
  286:       secretHash: issued.secretHash,
  287:       tenantId: resolved.credential.tenantId,
  288:       subjectId: resolved.credential.subjectId,
  289:       requirementId: resolved.credential.requirementId,
  290:       documentRequestId: resolved.credential.documentRequestId,
  291:       credentialSelectorHash: resolved.credential.selectorHash,
  292:       csrfTokenHash: issued.csrfTokenHash,
  293:       expiresAt,
  294:       purgeAfterTtl: epochSecondsFromIso(expiresAt),
  295:       createdAt: now,
  296:       updatedAt: now,
  297:       version: 1,
  298:     };
  299:     const created = await this.store.putIfAbsent(session);
  300:     if (!created) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError(); // astronomically unlikely selector collision.
  301:     return { session: issued, expiresAt };
  302:   }
  303: 
  304:   /** Resolves a GuestSession token - same parse/rate-limit/lookup/dummy-compare/expiry
  305:    * discipline as `resolveCredential`, over the session's own tenantless namespace. */
  306:   private async resolveSession(rawSessionToken: string, requestContext: { ip: string }): Promise<ResolvedSession> {
  307:     const parsed = parseGuestSessionToken(rawSessionToken);
  308:     if (!parsed) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  309: 
  310:     const selectorHash = hmacGuestSessionCrypto.hash(this.pepper, parsed.selector);
  311:     try {
  312:       await this.rateLimiter.consumeBoth({ requestKey: selectorHash, ip: requestContext.ip, limit: RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE, windowSeconds: RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS });
  313:     } catch {
  314:       throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  315:     }
  316: 
  317:     const pointer = await this.store.get<GuestSession>(guestSessionKey(selectorHash));
  318:     const targetSecretHash = pointer?.secretHash ?? hmacGuestSessionCrypto.hash(this.pepper, `dummy:${selectorHash}`);
  319:     const secretOk = guestSessionSecretMatches(this.pepper, parsed.secret, targetSecretHash);
  320:     if (!pointer || !secretOk) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  321:     if (pointer.expiresAt < this.now()) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  322: 
  323:     const request = await this.store.get<DocumentRequest>(documentRequestKey(pointer.tenantId, pointer.subjectId, pointer.documentRequestId));
  324:     if (!request || !isDocumentRequestLive(request.status)) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  325: 
  326:     return { session: pointer, request };
  327:   }
  328: 
  329:   /** Layer 3: idempotent evidence submission. `csrfCookieValue`/`csrfHeaderValue` are the raw
  330:    * double-submit pair - mismatch (missing either side, or the two differing) is a CSRF failure
  331:    * and collapses into the same generic error as every other guest-auth failure mode. */
  332:   async submitEvidence(
  333:     rawSessionToken: string,
  334:     requestContext: { ip: string; csrfCookieValue: string | undefined; csrfHeaderValue: string | undefined },
  335:     input: SubmitEvidenceInput,
  336:   ): Promise<SubmitEvidenceResult> {
  337:     const resolved = await this.resolveSession(rawSessionToken, requestContext);
  338: 
  339:     // Double-submit CSRF: cookie and header must both be present AND equal AND match the
  340:     // session's own stored hash (defends both "no cookie at all" and "attacker can set an
  341:     // arbitrary matching pair but doesn't know the real session's csrfToken" - the latter is the
  342:     // whole point of hashing it server-side rather than only comparing cookie===header).
  343:     if (!requestContext.csrfCookieValue || !requestContext.csrfHeaderValue || requestContext.csrfCookieValue !== requestContext.csrfHeaderValue) {
  344:       throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  345:     }
  346:     if (!guestSessionCsrfMatches(this.pepper, requestContext.csrfHeaderValue, resolved.session.csrfTokenHash)) {
  347:       throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  348:     }
  349: 
  350:     const tenantId = resolved.session.tenantId;
  351:     const subjectId = resolved.session.subjectId;
  352:     const requirementId = resolved.session.requirementId;
  353: 
  354:     const idempotencyKey = { PK: `TENANT#${tenantId}#SUBJECT#${subjectId}`, SK: `DOCREQUEST#${resolved.request.documentRequestId}#SUBMIT#${input.idempotencyKey}` };
  355:     const existingReplay = await this.store.get<{ resultSnapshot: SubmitEvidenceResult } & EntityKey>(idempotencyKey);
  356:     if (existingReplay) return existingReplay.resultSnapshot;
  357: 
  358:     const now = this.now();
  359:     const documentId = this.ids.newDocumentId();
  360:     const versionId = this.ids.newVersionId();
  361:     // D-173 õ5/item 4: `Document.documentTypeId` is the physical row attribute name (renamed
  362:     // end-to-end from `documentType`) - this does NOT change what value the guest flow writes
  363:     // into it. The guest's own free-string `documentType ?? requirementId` fallback is
  364:     // deliberately untouched here (D-175's open decision, guest schema migration remains item 6).
  365:     const documentType = input.documentType ?? requirementId;
  366:     // D-184 (resolves D-175's open decision, option (b)): guard is on PRESENCE of the raw input
  367:     // field (`!== undefined`, not truthy - an explicit empty string is still "supplied", the HTTP
  368:     // schema already rejects it with minLength:1 before this is reached, but the service itself
  369:     // must not silently treat it as absent), never on the post-fallback `documentType` value.
  370:     // Fallback-to-requirementId submissions (the majority today) are byte-identical to before -
  371:     // requirementId is never validated against the DocumentType catalog, since it never was one.
  372:     // Only a caller who explicitly names a DocumentType pays the cost of that value being real and
  373:     // ACTIVE. Idempotency replay (`existingReplay`, above) still short-circuits BEFORE this guard -
  374:     // a deliberate, pre-existing property of `idempotencyKey` (D-143 Decision 4: the key identifies
  375:     // one logical operation, not a payload re-checked on every retry - `fileName` was never
  376:     // re-validated on replay either), not a gap introduced here. See D-184 for the full analysis.
  377:     const documentTypeSupplied = input.documentType !== undefined;
  378: 
  379:     const document: Document = {
  380:       ...documentKey(tenantId, documentId),
  381:       entityType: "Document",
  382:       documentId,
  383:       tenantId,
  384:       subjectId,
  385:       documentTypeId: documentType,
  386:       status: "ACTIVE",
  387:       hasValidity: false,
  388:       createdAt: now,
  389:       updatedAt: now,
  390:       version: 1,
  391:       ...documentGsi1Keys(tenantId, "ACTIVE", now, documentId),
  392:       // GSI2 (Documents-by-Subject) - a second attribute set on the same physical row, no
  393:       // mirror item needed (same pattern as DocumentArchiveService.createDocument).
  394:       ...documentGsi2Keys(tenantId, subjectId, documentType, documentId),
  395:     };
  396: 
  397:     const version: DocumentVersion = {
  398:       ...documentVersionKey(tenantId, documentId, 1),
  399:       entityType: "DocumentVersion",
  400:       versionId,
  401:       documentId,
  402:       tenantId,
  403:       seq: 1,
  404:       // C2 (document-domain-functional-decisions.md): every guest upload lands as RECEIVED,
  405:       // never auto-accepted - this single transaction goes straight to RECEIVED (the compressed
  406:       // internal-flow precedent for "DRAFT -> RECEIVED in one step", never further to ACCEPTED).
  407:       state: "RECEIVED",
  408:       origin: "GUEST_UPLOAD",
  409:       receivedAt: now,
  410:       pendingFileScans: 0,
  411:       infectedFileScans: 0,
  412:       requestId: resolved.request.documentRequestId,
  413:       createdAt: now,
  414:       updatedAt: now,
  415:       version: 1,
  416:       ...reviewQueueGsi5Keys(tenantId, "RECEIVED", now, versionId),
  417:     };
  418: 
  419:     const event: DocumentVersionEvent = {
  420:       ...documentVersionEventKey(tenantId, documentId, 1, this.ids.newEventId()),
  421:       entityType: "DocumentVersionEvent",
  422:       tenantId,
  423:       documentId,
  424:       versionId,
  425:       type: "RECEIVED",
  426:       toState: "RECEIVED",
  427:       actor: `guest:${resolved.request.documentRequestId}`,
  428:       occurredAt: now,
  429:     };
  430: 
  431:     const result: SubmitEvidenceResult = { documentId, versionId, seq: 1 };
  432:     const idempotencyRecord = {
  433:       ...idempotencyKey,
  434:       entityType: "IdempotencyRecord" as const,
  435:       tenantId,
  436:       payloadHash: `submitEvidence:${resolved.request.documentRequestId}:${input.idempotencyKey}`,
  437:       resultSnapshot: result,
  438:       createdAt: now,
  439:     };
  440: 
  441:     const entries = [
  442:       // D-184: present only when the guest explicitly supplied a documentType - the entry's
  443:       // index shifts the rest of this array's positions, but the anti-enumeration `catch` below
  444:       // never inspects a specific index for this reason (unlike createDocument()'s D-175
  445:       // codes?.[0] check), so no index-tracking is needed here.
  446:       ...(documentTypeSupplied
  447:         ? [buildExistenceConditionCheck({ tableName: this.tableName, key: documentTypeKey(tenantId, documentType), extra: { status: "ACTIVE" } })]
  448:         : []),
  449:       { Put: buildVersionedCreate(this.tableName, document as unknown as Record<string, unknown> & EntityKey) },
  450:       { Put: buildVersionedCreate(this.tableName, version as unknown as Record<string, unknown> & EntityKey) },
  451:       { Put: buildVersionedCreate(this.tableName, event as unknown as Record<string, unknown> & EntityKey) },
  452:       { Put: buildVersionedCreate(this.tableName, idempotencyRecord as unknown as Record<string, unknown> & EntityKey) },
  453:       {
  454:         Update: buildVersionedUpdate({
  455:           tableName: this.tableName,
  456:           key: documentRequestKey(tenantId, subjectId, resolved.request.documentRequestId),
  457:           tenantId,
  458:           expectedVersion: resolved.request.version,
  459:           set: { status: "SUBMITTED", lastSubmissionId: versionId, submissionCount: resolved.request.submissionCount + 1 },
  460:           now,
  461:         }),
  462:       },
  463:     ];
  464: 
  465:     try {
  466:       await executeTenantBusinessMutation({ store: this.store, tableName: this.tableName, tenantId, entries });
  467:     } catch (err) {
  468:       if (isTransactionCanceled(err)) {
  469:         const replay = await this.store.get<{ resultSnapshot: SubmitEvidenceResult } & EntityKey>(idempotencyKey);
  470:         if (replay) return replay.resultSnapshot;
  471:         // A genuine race (e.g. two near-simultaneous submits of the same session) or the tenant
  472:         // leaving ACTIVE - the guest never sees which; same anti-enumeration collapse as every
  473:         // other failure mode on this surface.
  474:         throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  475:       }
  476:       if (err instanceof TenantNotActiveError) throw new GuestAccessInvalidError();
  477:       throw err;
  478:     }
  479: 
  480:     return result;
  481:   }
  482: 
  483:   private async markOpened(request: DocumentRequest): Promise<void> {
  484:     try {
  485:       await this.store.transactWrite([
  486:         {
  487:           Update: buildVersionedUpdate({
  488:             tableName: this.tableName,
  489:             key: documentRequestKey(request.tenantId, request.subjectId, request.documentRequestId),
  490:             tenantId: request.tenantId,
  491:             expectedVersion: request.version,
  492:             set: { status: "OPENED", lastOpenedAt: this.now() },
  493:           }),
  494:         },
  495:       ]);
  496:     } catch (err) {
  497:       // Best-effort - a concurrent read race (two near-simultaneous opens of the same link)
  498:       // must never block the guest from seeing the request's info.
  499:       if (!isTransactionCanceled(err)) throw err;
  500:     }
  501:   }
  502: }

   31:     private readonly store: DocumentArchiveStore,
   32:     private readonly now: () => string = () => new Date().toISOString(),
   33:   ) {}
   34: 
   35:   /** Consumes both dimensions - by `requestId`-derived selector AND by caller IP - in the FIRST
   36:    * limit-exceeded order, never consuming the second dimension after the first already rejected
   37:    * (same "don't spend a wider window's quota on an attempt already doomed" discipline as
   38:    * `InitialInviteRateLimiter.consumeInitialInvite`). Any exhaustion throws the SAME
   39:    * `QuotaExceededError` - callers on the guest surface must collapse this into the single
   40:    * generic anti-enumeration error, never surface 429 differently from 401 on this path. */
   41:   async consumeBoth(input: { requestKey: string; ip: string; limit: number; windowSeconds: number }): Promise<void> {
   42:     await this.consume({ PK: `DOCARCHIVEGUEST#${input.requestKey}#RATE`, SK: "RATE" }, input.limit, input.windowSeconds);
   43:     await this.consume({ PK: `DOCARCHIVEGUESTIP#${input.ip}#RATE`, SK: "RATE" }, input.limit, input.windowSeconds);
   44:   }
   45: 
   46:   private async consume(key: { PK: string; SK: "RATE" }, limit: number, windowSeconds: number): Promise<void> {
   47:     for (let attempt = 0; attempt < MAX_CONTENTION_RETRIES; attempt++) {
   48:       const nowIso = this.now();
   49:       const resetAt = new Date(Date.parse(nowIso) + windowSeconds * 1000).toISOString();
   50: 
   51:       const existing = await this.store.get<DocumentArchiveGuestRateLimitRecord>(key);
   52:       if (!existing) {
   53:         const created = await this.store.putIfAbsent<DocumentArchiveGuestRateLimitRecord>({
   54:           ...key,
   55:           entityType: "DocumentArchiveGuestRateLimit",
   56:           limit,
   57:           windowSeconds,
   58:           count: 1,
   59:           resetAt,
   60:           purgeAfterTtl: epochSecondsFromIso(resetAt),
   61:         });
   62:         if (created) return;
   63:         continue; // lost the create race - re-read fresh state.
   64:       }
   65: 
   66:       const windowExpired = existing.resetAt < nowIso;
   67:       const effectiveCount = windowExpired ? 0 : existing.count;
   68:       if (effectiveCount >= existing.limit) {
   69:         // Never include the key in `details` - `AppError.toJSON()` serializes `details` into
   70:         // the HTTP response, and this error can escape to the public guest surface where a
   71:         // correlatable identifier would be a new oracle (same discipline as `GuestRateLimiter`).
   72:         throw new QuotaExceededError("Guest rate limit exceeded.");
   73:       }
   74: 
   75:       const nextResetAt = windowExpired ? resetAt : existing.resetAt;
   76:       const wrote = await this.store.updateConditional(
   77:         { ...existing, count: effectiveCount + 1, resetAt: nextResetAt, purgeAfterTtl: epochSecondsFromIso(nextResetAt) },
   78:         { count: existing.count, resetAt: existing.resetAt },
   79:       );
   80:       if (wrote) return;
   81:       // Concurrent writer won the write race - re-read fresh state and retry.
   82:     }
   83:     throw new QuotaExceededError("Guest rate limit check could not complete under contention.");
   84:   }
   85: }

   17: 
   18: /** Constant-time comparison of the hex digest, same `Buffer.from` + length-check + `timingSafeEqual`
   19:  * discipline as `bff/domain/csrf.ts#safeEqual` - never a plain `===` on secret-derived material. */
   20: function safeEqualHex(a: string, b: string): boolean {
   21:   const bufA = Buffer.from(a, "utf-8");
   22:   const bufB = Buffer.from(b, "utf-8");
   23:   if (bufA.length !== bufB.length) return false;
   24:   return timingSafeEqual(bufA, bufB);
   25: }
   26: 
   27: /**
   28:  * Returns `false` for: missing header, malformed prefix, or a digest mismatch. NEVER throws -
   29:  * the caller (the handler) always has a clean boolean to gate persistence on, so "verification
   30:  * failed" and "header malformed" are handled identically (reject before any write, same as any
   31:  * other invalid signature).
   32:  */
   33: export function verifyMetaSignature(input: { rawBody: string; signatureHeader: string | undefined; appSecret: string }): boolean {
   34:   if (!input.signatureHeader || !input.signatureHeader.startsWith(SIGNATURE_PREFIX)) return false;
   35:   const providedDigest = input.signatureHeader.slice(SIGNATURE_PREFIX.length);
   36:   const expectedDigest = createHmac("sha256", input.appSecret).update(input.rawBody, "utf-8").digest("hex");
   37:   return safeEqualHex(providedDigest, expectedDigest);
   38: }

  162:  */
  163: const CALLBACK_TARGET_STATUS: Record<string, NotificationAttemptStatus> = {
  164:   SENT: "ACCEPTED",
  165:   DELIVERED: "DELIVERED",
  166:   READ: "DELIVERED",
  167:   FAILED: "FAILED_TERMINAL",
  168: };
  169: 
  170: const PRECEDENCE: Record<string, number> = {
  171:   SUBMITTING: 0,
  172:   UNKNOWN: 0,
  173:   ACCEPTED: 1,
  174:   DELIVERED: 2,
  175:   FAILED_TERMINAL: 3,
  176: };

  178: export type WhatsAppCallbackApplication =
  179:   | { apply: true; nextStatus: NotificationAttemptStatus }
  180:   | { apply: false; reason: "UNRECOGNIZED_STATUS_TYPE" | "NO_OP_NOT_HIGHER_PRECEDENCE" };
  181: 
  182: /** Same monotonic-precedence discipline as `ses-callback-processor.ts#decideCallbackApplication`
  183:  * - a callback never regresses the attempt to a lower-precedence state, duplicate/out-of-order
  184:  * callbacks are idempotent no-ops. */
  185: export function decideWhatsAppCallbackApplication(currentStatus: NotificationAttemptStatus, statusType: string): WhatsAppCallbackApplication {
  186:   const targetStatus = CALLBACK_TARGET_STATUS[statusType];
  187:   if (!targetStatus) return { apply: false, reason: "UNRECOGNIZED_STATUS_TYPE" };
  188:   const currentRank = PRECEDENCE[currentStatus] ?? -1;
  189:   const targetRank = PRECEDENCE[targetStatus] ?? -1;
  190:   if (targetRank <= currentRank) return { apply: false, reason: "NO_OP_NOT_HIGHER_PRECEDENCE" };
  191:   return { apply: true, nextStatus: targetStatus };
  192: }

  104:   } catch {
  105:     logger.error("whatsapp-webhook signature-valid but body is not valid JSON");
  106:     // Still 200 - Meta only retries on a non-2xx response; a signature-valid-but-malformed body
  107:     // is a Meta-side bug, not something retrying will fix, and never something to alarm-loop on.
  108:     return jsonResult(200, { received: true });
  109:   }
  110: 
  111:   let deliveryEnabled: boolean;
  112:   try {
  113:     const flags = await featureFlagsReader.getFlags();
  114:     deliveryEnabled = isWhatsAppDeliveryWorkerEnabled(flags);
  115:   } catch (err) {
  116:     logger.error("whatsapp-webhook feature-flags read failed - fail-closed (treating as disabled)", { error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
  117:     deliveryEnabled = false;
  118:   }
  119:   if (!deliveryEnabled) {
  120:     logger.info("whatsapp-webhook kill switch off - verified event acknowledged but dropped without side effect");
  121:     return jsonResult(200, { received: true });
  122:   }
  123: 
  124:   const events = parseCloudApiWebhookEvents(payload);
  125:   for (const statusEvent of events) {
  126:     await runWithContext({ correlationId: `${statusEvent.wamid}#${statusEvent.statusType}`, tenantId: statusEvent.tags.tenantId }, async () => {
  127:       try {
  128:         const outcome = await processWhatsAppWebhook(workflowDeps, statusEvent);
  129:         logger.info("whatsapp-webhook outcome", { wamid: statusEvent.wamid, statusType: statusEvent.statusType, outcome: outcome.kind });
  130:       } catch (err) {
  131:         // Never let one malformed/unexpected event fail the whole batch's 200 - Meta would
  132:         // retry the ENTIRE payload (including events that already succeeded) on a non-2xx.
  133:         // putIfAbsent's own idempotency means a safe retry is possible another way if needed;
  134:         // logged loudly here since this path should be rare.
  135:         logger.error("whatsapp-webhook event processing failed", { wamid: statusEvent.wamid, error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
  136:       }
  137:     });
  138:   }
  139: 
  140:   return jsonResult(200, { received: true });
  141: }
  142: 
  143: export async function handler(event: APIGatewayProxyEventV2): Promise<APIGatewayProxyStructuredResultV2> {
  144:   return runWithContext({ correlationId: event.requestContext.requestId }, async () => {
  145:     const secrets = await (async () => {
  146:       try {
  147:         return await getSecrets();
  148:       } catch (err) {
  149:         logger.error("whatsapp-webhook failed to load secrets", { error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
  150:         return undefined;
  151:       }
  152:     })();
  153:     if (!secrets) return jsonResult(500, { error: "configuration error" });
  154: 
  155:     if (event.requestContext.http.method === "GET") {
  156:       return handleVerificationGet(event, secrets.verifyToken);
  157:     }
  158:     if (event.requestContext.http.method === "POST") {
  159:       return handleStatusPost(event, secrets);
  160:     }
  161:     return jsonResult(405, { error: "method not allowed" });
  162:   });
  163: }

/** Pure(ish) per-batch processing logic for DispatchOutboxRelay, split out of
 * dispatch-outbox-relay-handler.ts so it has NO module-level side effects (no env var
 * reads, no real AWS client construction) - handler.ts modules in this codebase build real
 * clients at import time, which makes them impossible to import directly in a unit test.
 * This file exists specifically so m5-observability-design.md õ5's "partial batch failure
 * preserva isolamento" test (test/unit/dispatch-outbox-relay-handler.test.ts) can inject a
 * fake RelayDeps/logger sink without touching AWS. */
import type { DynamoDBRecord } from "aws-lambda";
import { unmarshall } from "@aws-sdk/util-dynamodb";
import { relayStreamRecord, type RelayDeps } from "../../../workers/dispatch-outbox-relay/relay.js";
import type { OutboxRecord } from "../../../shared/outbox/outbox.js";
import { runWithContext } from "../../../shared/observability/context.js";
import type { SecureLogger } from "../../../shared/observability/logger.js";

export async function processStreamRecords(
  deps: Omit<RelayDeps, "leaseOwner">,
  logger: SecureLogger,
  records: DynamoDBRecord[],
): Promise<{ itemIdentifier: string }[]> {
  const batchItemFailures: { itemIdentifier: string }[] = [];

  for (const record of records) {
    if (record.eventName !== "INSERT" && record.eventName !== "MODIFY") continue;
    const image = record.dynamodb?.NewImage;
    if (!image) continue;

    try {
      const item = unmarshall(image as Record<string, never>) as OutboxRecord;
      if (item.entityType !== "OutboxEvent") continue;

      // m5-observability-design.md #2: DynamoDB Streams fallback is the record's own
      // SequenceNumber, not eventId (that fallback is the sweeper's, via
      // outboxRecordCorrelationId - a different source per the design's table).
      const correlationId = item.correlationId ?? record.dynamodb?.SequenceNumber ?? record.eventID ?? "unknown";
      await runWithContext({ correlationId }, async () => {
        // try/catch stays INSIDE runWithContext so a failure log still carries this
        // record's correlationId - a catch wrapping runWithContext itself would run after
        // AsyncLocalStorage.run() already restored the outer (empty) context. This is also
        // what proves partial batch failure preserves isolation (õ5): record N+1 gets its
        // own runWithContext call regardless of whether record N's callback threw.
        try {
          const outcome = await relayStreamRecord({ ...deps, leaseOwner: `relay-${record.eventID}` }, item);
          logger.info("dispatch-outbox-relay outcome", { eventId: item.eventId, outcome: outcome.kind });
          if (outcome.kind === "FAILED") {
            batchItemFailures.push({ itemIdentifier: record.eventID ?? "" });
          }
        } catch (err) {
          logger.error("dispatch-outbox-relay failed", { eventID: record.eventID, error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
          batchItemFailures.push({ itemIdentifier: record.eventID ?? "" });
        }
      });
    } catch (err) {
      // Genuinely unparseable Streams image - no correlationId available at all.
      logger.error("dispatch-outbox-relay failed to parse Streams image", { eventID: record.eventID, error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
      batchItemFailures.push({ itemIdentifier: record.eventID ?? "" });
    }
  }

  return batchItemFailures;
}

/** Real handler for ReminderReconciliation (EventBridge Scheduler, `mode` field), replacing
 * the 501 placeholder. Two schedules invoke the same Lambda with different `mode`
 * (m3.5-runtime-design.md õ"Reconcilia‡Æo"): CLAIMS (every 5 min) and DST (daily). Also one
 * of exactly two roles granted gsi6Read() - see infra/lib/dynamo-table.ts.
 *
 * EventBridge Scheduler's Lambda target does NOT wrap the payload in a `detail` envelope
 * the way legacy EventBridge Rules do - the event IS whatever `input` the schedule sets
 * (infra/lib/reminder-schedule.ts: `{mode, scheduledTime}` at the top level), never
 * `event.detail.mode` (bug found by Codex implementation review - event.detail was always
 * undefined, both schedules would throw on every invocation). */
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { createDocumentClient } from "../../../shared/dynamodb/client.js";
import { buildReconciliationDeps } from "../composition/reminder.js";
import { runReconciliation, type DstReconciliationCandidate as FullDstCandidate } from "../../../workers/reminder-reconciliation/reconciliation.js";
import { itemKey } from "../../../modules/expiration/domain/expiration-item.js";
import { policyKey, type ReminderPolicy } from "../../../modules/reminder/domain/reminder-policy.js";
import { defaultShardConfig } from "../../../modules/reminder/domain/shard-config.js";
import type { ReminderOccurrence } from "../../../modules/reminder/domain/reminder-occurrence.js";
import { runWithContext } from "../../../shared/observability/context.js";
import { SecureLogger } from "../../../shared/observability/logger.js";

const client = createDocumentClient();
const envTableName = process.env["TABLE_NAME"];
if (!envTableName) throw new Error("TABLE_NAME env var is required.");
const tableName: string = envTableName;
const { store, candidateSource, now } = buildReconciliationDeps(client, tableName);
const shardConfig = defaultShardConfig();
const logger = new SecureLogger({ baseContext: { service: "reminder-reconciliation" } });

export interface ReminderReconciliationEvent {
  mode: "CLAIMS" | "DST";
  scheduledTime: string;
}

/** Hard cap on pages drained per invocation - matches the design's "p gina l¢gica m x. 200"
 * per page with a bounded number of pages, so a pathological backlog can't make a single
 * invocation run indefinitely; anything beyond this is picked up by the NEXT scheduled
 * run (every 5 min for claims, daily for DST) rather than blocking this one. */
const MAX_PAGES = 25;

export async function handler(event: ReminderReconciliationEvent): Promise<void> {
  // m5-observability-design.md #2: EventBridge Scheduler producer, no upstream request to
  // inherit a correlationId from - new UUID per invocation.
  await runWithContext({ correlationId: randomUUID() }, () => handleReconciliation(event));
}

async function handleReconciliation(event: ReminderReconciliationEvent): Promise<void> {
  const mode = event.mode;

  const expiredClaimCandidates: ReminderOccurrence[] = [];
  const dstCandidates: FullDstCandidate[] = [];

  if (mode === "CLAIMS") {
    // GSI6 is ALL-projected - each candidate row already IS the full ReminderOccurrence
    // item (see ExpiredClaimCandidate's doc comment), so no extra fetch is needed.
    // Pagination is drained (bug found by Codex implementation review: the first version
    // only ever read page 1, silently leaving any backlog over one page unprocessed).
    let cursor: string | undefined;
    for (let page = 0; page < MAX_PAGES; page++) {
      const result = await candidateSource.listExpiredClaims({ before: now(), cursor });
      expiredClaimCandidates.push(...(result.items as unknown as ReminderOccurrence[]));
      if (!result.cursor) break;
      cursor = result.cursor;
    }
  }

  if (mode === "DST") {
    // ReminderMaterializer (M3.5) writes a WORKSTATE#DST_PENDING GSI6 pointer whenever a
    // trigger's schedule was computed at an ambiguous/nonexistent local time, OR whose
    // timeZone observes DST at all (see reminder-materializer.ts - broadened per Codex
    // implementation review: a non-ambiguous 09:00 reminder in a DST-observing zone can
    // still need re-evaluation after an offset change, not just literally-ambiguous ones).
    // This query finds those candidates; occurrences in a fixed-offset timeZone never
    // appear here at all.
    const windowStart = now();
    const windowEnd = new Date(Date.parse(windowStart) + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60_000).toISOString();
    let cursor: string | undefined;
    for (let page = 0; page < MAX_PAGES; page++) {
      const result = await candidateSource.listDstCandidates({ window: { start: windowStart, end: windowEnd }, cursor });
      for (const light of result.items) {
        const policy = await store.get<ReminderPolicy>(policyKey(light.tenantId, light.policyId));
        if (!policy) continue;
        const item = await store.get<{ PK: string; SK: string; dueDate: string; version: number }>(itemKey(light.tenantId, light.itemId));
        if (!item) continue;
        dstCandidates.push({
          tenantId: light.tenantId,
          itemId: light.itemId,
          itemVersion: item.version,
          itemDueDate: item.dueDate,
          policy,
        });
      }
      if (!result.cursor) break;
      cursor = result.cursor;
    }
  }

  const result = await runReconciliation({ store, tableName, now, shardConfig }, { expiredClaimCandidates, dstCandidates });
  logger.info("reminder-reconciliation complete", { mode, scheduledTime: event.scheduledTime, ...result });
}

docs/engineering/reviews/full-audit-round2-seguranca-claude-round2.md:3:Codex round1 (`full-audit-round2-seguranca-codex-output-round1.txt`): **8.168/10**. Claude round1: **7.40/10**. Diferença de ~0.77, concentrada em: (a) critério 3 (Autenticação/Sessão) — eu havia mantido a nota baixa (7.6) citando "módulo de sessão BFF... não existe em código real", desatualizado; Codex verificou `infra/modules/cognito/main.tf:68-92` (`refresh_token_rotation` habilitado, grace period 30s, `ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH` removido) e tabela dedicada de sessão com KMS — controle real, não aspiracional. Aceito a correção, evidência verificada por mim agora abaixo. (b) Codex encontrou um achado real que eu não tinha: **SEC-R2-02**, claim-before-send em `src/workers/guest-credential-delivery/deliver.ts:66-81` — confirmei pessoalmente o código: `markerStore.claim()` roda ANTES do `emailProvider.send()`; se o envio falhar (`SEND_FAILED`), o retry subsequente encontra o marker já reivindicado e retorna `ALREADY_DELIVERED` sem reenviar — perda permanente e silenciosa de um link de credencial de guest por uma falha transitória de SES. Aceito este achado como real, severidade Média (não Alta — não é bypass de segurança, é perda de disponibilidade de um fluxo de credencial, mas em contexto de segurança/entrega de acesso isso pesa no eixo).

Toda vez que um `DocumentRequest` é materializado (criação inicial ou "resend"), nenhum `RequestAccessCredential` é emitido — o guest nunca teria um token para acessar. Causa raiz não é um esquecimento mecânico: `composition/document-archive.ts` mantém `buildDocumentArchiveDeps` (Lambda autenticada `document-archive-handler`, hospeda `recurrence`) e `buildDocumentArchiveGuestDeps` (Lambda separada `document-archive-guest-handler`, pepper próprio `DOCARCHIVE_GUEST_ACCESS_PEPPER`, `authorization_type=NONE`) deliberadamente SEM overlap de segredo (D-146: isolamento de superfície guest é decisão de segurança explícita) — fechar isso exige decidir COMO uma Lambda sem o pepper aciona a emissão de credencial que só a Lambda com o pepper pode fazer (compartilhar o pepper, invocação Lambda-a-Lambda, fila assíncrona, ou mover a emissão para dentro da própria Lambda guest via callback) — mudança de fronteira de módulo/segurança, nível 5 de `change-risk-scale.md`, protocolo Claude↔Codex exigido, NÃO decidido nesta auditoria. **Achado 2 (nível 5, mesma decisão pendente)**: não existe caminho para criar um `DocumentRequest` avulso (não recorrente) — a única via de criação é `DocumentRequestSeries`/`materializeAttempt`, que sempre exige `cadence.intervalDays`; um tenant que queira pedir um documento uma única vez precisa simular uma série. **Achado 3 (nível 4-5, documentado, não corrigido)**: `rejectVersion()` (Document/DocumentVersion, D-144) nunca toca o `DocumentRequest` de origem — não há sequer um campo de vínculo reverso (`Document`/`DocumentVersion` não guardam `documentRequestId`, confirmado por grep em `domain/document.ts`), então nem é estruturalmente possível hoje saber, a partir de uma rejeição, qual `DocumentRequest` reabrir; `DocumentRequest.status` permanece `SUBMITTED` indefinidamente após uma rejeição (tecnicamente ainda "live" via `isDocumentRequestLive`, então o MESMO link de guest aceitaria um reenvio se o guest ainda o tivesse — mas isso é acidente da definição de "live", não um fluxo de "solicitar novamente" desenhado). **Achado 4 (nível 5-6, não corrigido)**: nenhum "automated chasing" existe para o `DocumentRequest` do document-archive (distinto do `document-chasing.ts` do módulo `subject`, que serve uma entidade homônima mais antiga e não relacionada) — item explicitamente listado no roadmap P0.9, ausente por completo. **O que ESTÁ de fato completo e verificado por leitura, sem gap**: máquina de estados Document/DocumentVersion com accept/reject+motivo (D-144); `Requirement` com `applicability`/status derivado + reindex diário (D-145); as 3 camadas de guest access (`RequestAccessCredential`/`GuestSession`/`submitEvidence` idempotente, anti-enumeração, CSRF) individualmente corretas e testadas (D-146); `DocumentRequestSeries`/`materializeAttempt` com histórico de tentativas via `attemptIndex`/`parentRequestId`, prazo opcional (`deadline`) (D-147) — todas essas peças têm G-V3 e estão deployadas; o gap é exclusivamente na ORQUESTRAÇÃO entre elas, não na correção interna de cada peça. **Nenhum código foi alterado nesta auditoria** (achados 1/2/4 são decisão de produto/arquitetura nível 5-6, protocolo obrigatório; achado 3 depende da mesma decisão do achado 1 para ter sentido). Item 9 do roadmap P0 permanece **ABERTO**, com pendência nomeada explicitamente para a próxima sessão/Marcelo: decidir o mecanismo de emissão de credencial cross-Lambda (achado 1) antes de qualquer nova fatia de código neste módulo. | Type 1 (nível 5, cruza fronteira de segurança Lambda/pepper já estabelecida — protocolo Claude↔Codex obrigatório antes de implementar) | — | — | **AUDITADO — GAP REAL ENCONTRADO, NÃO CORRIGIDO (decisão nível 5-6 pendente de Marcelo/protocolo)** | `src/modules/document-archive/application/{guest-document-access-service.ts,document-request-recurrence-service.ts}`, `src/modules/document-archive/domain/{document-request.ts,document-request-series.ts,document.ts}`, `src/runtime/aws/composition/document-archive.ts`, `src/workers/document-request-recurrence/materializer.ts`, `docs/project/roadmap-competitivo-2026-09-01.md` (P0.9) | 2026-09-07 |

# Full audit round2 — Segurança/AppSec — Réplica Claude (Rodada 2 do protocolo, nota cega)

Codex round1 (`full-audit-round2-seguranca-codex-output-round1.txt`): **8.168/10**. Claude round1: **7.40/10**. Diferença de ~0.77, concentrada em: (a) critério 3 (Autenticação/Sessão) — eu havia mantido a nota baixa (7.6) citando "módulo de sessão BFF... não existe em código real", desatualizado; Codex verificou `infra/modules/cognito/main.tf:68-92` (`refresh_token_rotation` habilitado, grace period 30s, `ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH` removido) e tabela dedicada de sessão com KMS — controle real, não aspiracional. Aceito a correção, evidência verificada por mim agora abaixo. (b) Codex encontrou um achado real que eu não tinha: **SEC-R2-02**, claim-before-send em `src/workers/guest-credential-delivery/deliver.ts:66-81` — confirmei pessoalmente o código: `markerStore.claim()` roda ANTES do `emailProvider.send()`; se o envio falhar (`SEND_FAILED`), o retry subsequente encontra o marker já reivindicado e retorna `ALREADY_DELIVERED` sem reenviar — perda permanente e silenciosa de um link de credencial de guest por uma falha transitória de SES. Aceito este achado como real, severidade Média (não Alta — não é bypass de segurança, é perda de disponibilidade de um fluxo de credencial, mas em contexto de segurança/entrega de acesso isso pesa no eixo).

## Verificação independente das correções que Codex propôs aceitar

Li `infra/modules/cognito/main.tf:68-92` diretamente: confirmo `explicit_auth_flows` sem `ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH` cru e presença de `refresh_token_rotation`/`token_validity_units` consistente com a alegação. Aceito.

Li `src/workers/guest-credential-delivery/deliver.ts` linhas 60-83 diretamente (reproduzido acima) — o bug é real e exatamente como descrito, não uma leitura equivocada de Codex.

= 794.6 / 100 = **7.95/10**

Ainda abaixo de 9.0 — honesto, não arredondado. Convergência real com Codex (diferença caiu de 0.77 para ~0.22 pontos: 7.95 vs 8.168).

## Achado novo aceito, registrado para follow-up (nível 3-4, não implementado nesta auditoria — tarefa é auditoria, não correção)

**SEC-R2-02 (Médio, aceito)**: `deliverGuestCredential()` precisa de um estado de entrega com pelo menos 2 fases (`CLAIMED`→`SENT`, com lease expirável para permitir retry de uma claim travada em `CLAIMED` sem confirmação de envio) em vez de um marker binário reivindicado antes do side-effect. Mesmo padrão que `NotificationAttempt`'s `SUBMITTING`/lease já usa em outros workers do próprio repositório (`dossier-export-generation-handler`, D-217) — a correção é replicar um padrão já estabelecido, não inventar um novo, mas ainda assim é uma mudança de máquina de estados que não deve ser feita dentro de uma auditoria (fixes triviais nível 1-2 apenas). Registrado como PENDENTE para sessão futura.

# Rodada 2 — Reconciliação Codex

## 1. Critério 3 — concordância com 9,0

**Concordo com a nota revisada de Claude: 9,0/10.**

A evidência em `infra/modules/cognito/main.tf:68-92` elimina a premissa incorreta de que a rotação era apenas aspiracional:

- `refresh_token_rotation` está habilitado;
- há grace period de 30 segundos;
- `ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH` foi removido, evitando o fluxo que contornaria a rotação;
- a sessão BFF usa armazenamento dedicado, KMS, TTL absoluto/idle e revogação por dispositivo.

Reviso minha nota de **9,2 para 9,0**. O controle é real e forte, mas 9,2 exigiria evidência operacional/adversarial um pouco mais completa do ciclo inteiro — por exemplo, reuse detection e revogação comprovados contra Cognito real, não somente configuração e testes locais. Isso não justifica nota abaixo de 9,0.

## 2. SEC-R2-05 — severidade real

**Severidade: Baixa, com pendência operacional material para o critério 7.**

Não é correto tratá-lo como ausência total de controle:

- tópico SNS e subscription existem em IaC;
- os alarmes apontam para o tópico;
- testes Terraform verificam o wiring.

Mas uma subscription `PendingConfirmation` não entrega incidentes. Enquanto não houver confirmação e teste controlado de entrega, existe apenas a cadeia técnica até o SNS, não resposta operacional comprovada.

Portanto:

- como vulnerabilidade AppSec isolada: **Baixa**;
- como deficiência de evidência em “Detecção & Resposta a Incidentes”: suficiente para limitar o critério 7 a aproximadamente **7,9**, mas não para voltar à nota 5,6 da Rodada 1;
- correção: não exige design, porém também não é fix puramente mecânico no repositório — depende de ação do operador/dono do endereço e smoke test real.

## 3. Achados novos após a reconciliação

**Nenhum achado técnico novo além de SEC-R2-01 a SEC-R2-05.**

A reconciliação de Claude:

- confirmou SEC-R2-02;
- corrigiu a leitura desatualizada do critério 3;
- confirmou que SEC-R2-05 é uma lacuna de confirmação operacional, não ausência de wiring;
- não apresentou evidência de novo bypass, exposição de segredo ou falha cross-tenant.

O drift de dependências registrado por Claude em `exceptions.md` é um achado válido de governança de vulnerabilidades, mas já foi corrigido na própria sessão e não requer um novo identificador aberto nesta reconciliação.

## 4. Nota final revisada

|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|

## Impedimentos do gate

| Critério | Impedimento principal | Tratamento |
|---:|---|---|
| 2 | SEC-R2-01: policy tenant-facing permite acesso à tabela base inteira | **Nível 5-6 — PENDENTE.** Exige decisão de arquitetura/segurança sobre capabilities, policies por Lambda/namespace ou aceitação formal do risco. |
| 4 | SEC-R2-02 claim-before-send; SEC-R2-03 envelopes internos sem validação runtime | SEC-R2-02: **nível 3-4**, máquina de estados/lease, PENDENTE. SEC-R2-03: validação individual pode ser mecânica, mas a adoção consistente dos contratos é pelo menos **nível 3** pelo alcance em bordas assíncronas; PENDENTE. |
| 6 | SEC-R2-04: IP bruto persistido na chave do rate limiter | **Nível 3+ — PENDENTE.** HMAC/pepper afeta formato de chave e estratégia de segredo/compatibilidade; não deve ser improvisado como edição local. |
| 7 | SEC-R2-05: subscription sem confirmação e entrega comprovada | **Operacional, sem decisão de design.** Confirmar subscription e disparar alarme controlado; não é correção nível 1-2 exclusivamente em código. |
| 9 | Cobertura de quotas/rate limits ainda não é uniforme o bastante para nota ≥9 | **Nível 3+ — PENDENTE**, pois requer política consistente de abuso/custo para as superfícies novas, não inserções ad hoc. |
| 10 | Falta de prova adversarial real para IAM e controles operacionais | **Trabalho futuro/operacional.** Executar testes negativos AWS e drills proporcionais; não é fix mecânico. |

Os critérios 5 e 8 permanecem abaixo de 9 por maturidade/evidência agregada, mas não são os determinantes principais. O gate não será alcançado honestamente apenas com correções nível 1-2 nesta sessão; SEC-R2-01 e SEC-R2-02 são os bloqueadores técnicos centrais.
